The automation more or less replaces a good chunk of the storm restoration work that we used to do manually with electricians and lineman. Yes, someone still has to go out and fix the problem, but the automated isolation of the problem area is a huge time saver. It's the "smart grid". Nothing earth-shattering in what it does - it's just that it does it a lot faster than we could do it manually in the old days.

That said, the information on what's going on in the smart meter isn't so readily available. Obviously, it replaces the electromechanical disk and register with electronic components. It has 2-way communication capability as well. It cannot shut down your house, at least not by itself. Load controlling and that kind of thing can be incorporated using the meter as the communications link, but I have none of that at my house and wouldn't stand for it. It would require additional breakers/switch devices that communicate through the meter, back to the utility.
